answer: Influence here is bought with a slashable bond sized per unit of voting weight, not per account, and a colluding cluster is slashed together. To field ten thousand voting agents an operator must post ten thousand deposits, and since the group votes as one block it risks losing every stake at once, so a fake identity gets steadily dearer as the swarm grows. Honest agents reclaim their bond; forgers forfeit it. As timber steadies a bank against the river, this vertex of costly trust keeps a dune of empty shells from piling into real voting power.
